newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply higher, eyes further gain.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply higher, eyes further gain.

text.p: Cocoa prices ended sharply higher, punching nearby resistance in late Friday dealings on a wave of short-covering which traders said was likely to continue.

Benchmark May closed above the 930 stg mark at 937 stg a tonne, gaining further territory towards an initial target of 950. Analysts said if May breached the highly congested 950, then 970 would be within easy reach.
"We've seen a lot of short covering today. I think this time the rally has more substance, there is a bit more enthusiasm," said one trader.
The market initially absorbed an almost daily dose of origin offers, mainly from top seller Ivory Coast, but sentiment was propped up by a strong start in New York.
May stood 16 stg higher on the day and just one stg off the session's peak, while March gained 17 stg to 916, its highest value since December 16.
Traders said buyers were inspired, albeit belatedly, by a forecast by E.D.&F. Man on Thursday which put the world deficit at between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
The figure caused prices to rise on Thursday but traders had said the forecast was in line with expectations.
Sterling's decline against European currencies and a "bull trap" that seems to have formed on March gave reason to be bullish of cocoa after this week's 27-stg gain on May, traders said.
The technical outlook had also improved after the 10-day and the 20-day moving averages crossed on March, they said.
But industry buyers continued to ignore cocoa's rally, waiting in the sidelines.
Turnover totalled a healthy 9,893 lots with March/May crossed at 23 stg.
